full_judgment: 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the schedule 3 land to the plaint belonged to Hafez Ali Akbar who entered into an oral contract for sale of the said land for a consideration of Taka 26,000 in favour of the plaintiff in the month of Baishak 1362. Said Hafez Ali Akbar on receipt of entire consideration money handed over possession of the said land in favour of the plaintiff who started possessing the land and during his possession Hafez Ali Akbar died in the year 1965 leaving behind the defendant Nos. 1-9 as his heirs. During possession of the plaintiff the SA Khatian in respect of the said land was prepared in his name and he also paid rent and had been in possession more than 12 years. The plaintiff requested the defendant Nos. 1-9 to execute and register a sale deed pursuant to the said oral contract but they refused. By virtue of continuous possession for more than 12 years there was created title by adverse possession in favour of the plaintiff as against the defendants. Thereafter, the plaintiff came to know that the defendant Nos. 1-5 had executed and registered a sale deed in respect of schedule 3 land to the plaint dated 6-6-1980 in favour of the defendant Nos. 10-13 (the present petitioner). Thereafter, the plaintiff instituted the instant suit being No. 206 of 1980 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Chandpur for declaration of title by way of adverse possession and for further declaration that the deed dated 6-6-1980 executed by the defendants Nos. 1-5 in favour of the defendants Nos. 10-13 to be void, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff, that the suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 182 of 1982.
